name: Shenazzar
title: Son of King Jeconiah in captivity
summary: Shenazzar was a son of Jeconiah (Jehoiachin), the last king of Judah who was taken into exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in the royal genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles and is part of the messianic lineage. Some scholars have attempted to identify him with Sheshbazzar, the prince who led the first group of returning Jews from Babylon, but this remains debated.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Jeconiah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Shenazzar is listed among the sons of King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) who were born during the Babylonian exile. This places him within the royal Davidic lineage.

keyEvents.title: Jeconiah's Exile in Babylon
keyEvents.description: Shenazzar's father, King Jeconiah, was taken into exile in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC. It was during this exile that Shenazzar was born.

keyEvents.title: The Royal Davidic Line Preserved
keyEvents.description: Despite the Davidic royal family being in exile, the lineage was maintained through Jeconiah's sons, including Shenazzar, which was vital for messianic hope.

keyEvents.title: Jeconiah's Restoration in Exile
keyEvents.description: King Evil-Merodach of Babylon released Jeconiah from prison and gave him a place of honor. This improved conditions for the entire royal family, including Shenazzar.

keyEvents.title: Possible Connection to Sheshbazzar
keyEvents.description: Some scholars identify Shenazzar with Sheshbazzar, the prince commissioned by the Persian king Cyrus to bring the temple vessels back to Jerusalem and lead the first return.
